reviewer.impersonation_disclaimer: Not a human reviewer. Issued under the owner governance amendment with requires_release_gate_amendment=true.
reviewer.method: read-only static review plus four independent executions of the registered test gates on the registered host. No ledger, destination, attempt, or real execution was created; nothing one-shot was consumed.

part_1_what_passed_review.commit_shape: single parent be64235, exactly the five preregistered A paths, digests as reported
part_1_what_passed_review.shim: imports only os and sys, hand-implements SHA-256 to avoid earlier imports, zero authority state, zero validator references, 293 lines
part_1_what_passed_review.implementation_module: rejects direct __main__ at line 21 before any authority exists; sole owner of both ContextVars
part_1_what_passed_review.validator: imports the implementation module, never the shim; shim path appears only as data strings
part_1_what_passed_review.identity_proofs: id()-based ContextVar and module-object equality checks present in code as preregistered
part_1_what_passed_review.static_gates_rerun_by_reviewer: ruff clean, strict mypy clean on the three sources, py_compile clean
part_1_what_passed_review.disclosed_probe_reproduced: the operator's voluntarily disclosed non-registered probe of strict mypy over the two test files reproduces at exactly 19 findings, all test-scaffolding type-narrowing; agreed not a blocker
part_1_what_passed_review.in_process_tests: 238 of 252 pass, including every identity, ledger-formula, tamper-matrix, carry-forward and schema test that does not spawn the full exact-OS pipeline
part_1_what_passed_review.fast_exact_os_paths: bootstrap-to-rejection tests pass quickly, e.g. the missing-action-receipt rejection, so the exec chain itself works

part_2_the_blocker.statement: The registered acceptance claim of 252/252 passing is not reproducible by the independent reviewer on the registered host. Fourteen tests, thirteen errors and one failure, share a single root cause: the exact-OS full-pipeline child produces no output within its embedded 300-second budget and is killed.
part_2_the_blocker.error_shape: subprocess.TimeoutExpired after 300.0 seconds with stdout='' and stderr='', child killed with returncode -9 by the test harness; the one FAILED test asserts 'exact-OS child timed out' with the same empty output
reproduction_evidence: attempt 1, secondary worktree, suite: same error family at the same positions before being killed by a tool limit
attempt 2, secondary worktree, suite: 59 passes then the error block, then wedged
attempt 3, registered root at detached cf10ef8, full suite to completion: 238 passed, 13 errors, 1 failure, all timeouts

attempt 4, decisive: one affected test run alone on a quiet host took 501 seconds total, its child exceeded the 300-second budget with zero output while consuming roughly twenty percent CPU, working rather than deadlocked
part_2_the_blocker.discrepancy_with_operator_report: The operator reported Runner 150/150 and Validator 102/102 including the full-shape series tests. Four reviewer executions on the same machine contradict that. This review does not assert the operator's report was false; it asserts the gate does not reproduce for the reviewer, and an acceptance gate that passes only in one party's environment is not yet a gate.

part_3_ruled_out_by_measurement.note: recorded to save remediation time and to correct the reviewer's own interim guesses
part_3_ruled_out_by_measurement.shim_hash_speed: the hand-written SHA-256 measures 849 KB/s and both pinned binaries are about 151 KB, so shim hashing costs under one second; the reviewer's earlier hypothesis that it was the bottleneck is disproven
part_3_ruled_out_by_measurement.worktree_path_pinning: the reviewer's earlier statement that the tests reject foreign directories was wrong; the exact-OS tests build fully synthetic project roots under pytest temp and behave identically in both locations
part_3_ruled_out_by_measurement.database_contention: the real-path fingerprint set covers five protected paths and not the live database, so P4.1 polling cannot break the fixtures
part_3_ruled_out_by_measurement.deadlock: the child shows steady partial CPU and its subprocess tree keeps changing, so it is slow, not stuck
part_3_ruled_out_by_measurement.reviewer_load_contamination: excluded by attempt 4, run alone on a quiet host

part_4_what_is_required_to_clear: Explain the reproducibility gap: under what measured conditions did the operator's run pass, including per-test wall-clock for the exact-OS family.

Profile where the child spends its budget and either make it fit 300 seconds, or raise the embedded test budgets with a stated justification and the resulting suite duration, or register an explicit environmental precondition for the gate. Any of these changes the five-path surface and therefore requires a new commit descending from cf10ef8 and a fresh independent review.
The suite-context-only error of the launcher-bytes test, which passes alone, must also be explained by the remediation, since it suggests cross-test interference within the exact-OS family.
Nothing was consumed. Under DISCLOSED_REPEATABLE_SERIES_V1 this costs exactly one review cycle, which is the design working as intended.
